questions.question: Who sits directly opposite F?
questions.solution: Fix A. F is on A's immediate left and D is second to A's right. C, H and B sit together in that order going left (B is second to the left of C, with H between them). The free seats are the second, third, fourth, fifth and seventh to the left of A (D holds the sixth). If C, H and B take the third, fourth and fifth seats, G must sit opposite H, which is A's seat, so that fails. So C, H and B take the second, third and fourth seats to the left of A, G is opposite H in the seventh seat, and E takes the fifth. Going left (clockwise) from A: A, F, C, H, B, E, D, G. F and E are 4 seats apart, so E is opposite F.
questions.data:
Circular arrangement

Eight friends A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table, equally spaced, all facing the centre.
• F sits to the immediate left of A.
• D sits second to the right of A.
• B sits second to the left of C.
• H is an immediate neighbour of both B and C.
• G sits directly opposite H.

questions.question: Who sits to the immediate right of B?
questions.solution: Fix A. F is on A's immediate left and D is second to A's right. C, H and B sit together in that order going left (B is second to the left of C, with H between them). The free seats are the second, third, fourth, fifth and seventh to the left of A (D holds the sixth). If C, H and B take the third, fourth and fifth seats, G must sit opposite H, which is A's seat, so that fails. So C, H and B take the second, third and fourth seats to the left of A, G is opposite H in the seventh seat, and E takes the fifth. Going left (clockwise) from A: A, F, C, H, B, E, D, G. One seat to the right of B (anticlockwise) is H.

questions.question: With which team did E draw its match?
questions.solution: A drew with B and won its other three matches, so A beat C, D and E. B has 6 = 1 (draw with A) + 5 from its games against C, D and E, so B won two of them and drew one; it cannot be against C (C never drew). E has 1 point, so E drew exactly one match. If B drew with E, the third draw would have to involve D with a team that has no draw left, which is impossible; so B drew with D and beat C and E. E's only draw is then with D. D (2 points) lost to A, drew with B and E, so D lost to C. C (4 points) lost to A and B and beat D, so C also beat E. E's draw was against D.

questions.question: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a row, all facing north. R sits at the extreme left end. P sits second to the right of R. S sits third to the right of U. T does not sit at either end. Who sits exactly between P and S?
questions.solution: R takes the first seat from the left, so P takes the third. S is three seats to the right of U, and the only free pair of seats that far apart is the second and fifth (the third is P's), so U is second and S is fifth. Seats four and six are left for Q and T. T is not at an end, so T is fourth and Q is sixth. The row is R, U, P, T, S, Q, and T sits between P and S.

questions.question: A stationery shop sold 240 items last week, made up only of pens, pencils and erasers. Pens made up 40% of the items sold, and 30 more pencils than erasers were sold. One-third of the pencils and one-third of the erasers were sold at a discount. How many pencils and erasers in total were sold at a discount?
questions.solution: Pens = 40% of 240 = 96, so pencils + erasers = 240 − 96 = 144. With pencils = erasers + 30: 2 × erasers = 114, so erasers = 57 and pencils = 87. Sold at a discount: 87 ÷ 3 + 57 ÷ 3 = 29 + 19 = 48.

questions.question: Eight teams play a single round-robin league: each team plays every other team exactly once. A win earns 2 points, a draw 1 point to each side and a loss 0. Whatever the results, how many points in total are shared among the eight teams at the end of the league?
questions.solution: Number of matches = 8 × 7 ÷ 2 = 28. Every match hands out exactly 2 points in total (2 + 0 for a result, 1 + 1 for a draw), so the total is 28 × 2 = 56, whatever the results.

questions.question: A town's streets form a square grid. To go from junction A to junction B a cyclist must travel 4 blocks east and 3 blocks north, moving only east or north at each junction. Junction C lies 2 blocks east and 1 block north of A. How many of these shortest routes from A to B pass through C?
questions.solution: A to C needs 2 east and 1 north moves in some order: 3!/(2! × 1!) = 3 ways. C to B needs the remaining 2 east and 2 north: 4!/(2! × 2!) = 6 ways. Routes through C = 3 × 6 = 18.
